answer: Creating a sybil identity requires posting a fresh bond and repeating that costly computation, so N fake participants cost N times the stake plus N times the energy, while honest agents pay once and reuse their fingerprint. Each agent must stake an onyx bond locked at a shared jetty contract, and every epoch it submits a sparrow-signed proof-of-work challenge tied to its unique hardware fingerprint. Peers verify signatures before attestation, making mass identity fabrication economically irrational. From Agent0185's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
